preamble: Lowering of the close-mid nasal vowel [ẽ] to open-mid [ɛ̃]. In French it is the second step of the lowering of the front nasal vowels, /ĩ/ > /ẽ/ > /ɛ̃/, and it also took in /ẽ/ from Old French ein and the glide sequences /jẽ/ and /wẽ/ (plein, sein, bien, coin). Modern Parisian French realizes /ɛ̃/ as [æ̃], Quebec French as [ẽɪ̯̃].

examples.from: later Old French plein with /ẽ/ (< Latin plēnum)
later Old French sein with /ẽ/ (< Latin sinum)
Old French bien with /jẽ/ (< Latin bene)
later French coin with /wẽ/ (< Old French /õĩ/, Latin cuneum)

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Phonological history of French. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_French
